answer: An outdoor activity I thoroughly enjoy is hiking, particularly in the hill areas of Sylhet and Bandarban. Sirajganj itself is completely flat, so I usually go on a trip once or twice a year, often during the cooler winter months when the trails are dry. I usually go with a small group of close friends from university, which makes it even more enjoyable. We share the planning, travel overnight by bus and stay in simple guesthouses, which is all part of the adventure. What I love about it is the wonderful combination of exercise, fresh air and stunning scenery. After months of office work and busy roads, spending a few days in nature is genuinely [[rejuvenating]]. There is something deeply satisfying about reaching the top of a trail after a challenging climb and being rewarded with a [[breathtaking]] view. In Bandarban, you can sometimes stand above the clouds in the early morning, which I will never forget. Honestly, I find hiking to be both physically and mentally [[restorative]]; it clears my head like nothing else. It is also a great way to bond with friends, away from the distractions of daily life, as the phone signal is often weak anyway. I think spending time in nature is something modern life sorely lacks, and hiking is my favourite way to reconnect with it. Between trips, I make do with long walks along the river at home. I always return home feeling tired but genuinely [[content]]. It is easily one of my favourite ways to spend a holiday, and I am already counting down to our next [[excursion]].

followUps.q: Does your family worry when you go hiking?
followUps.answer: My mother certainly does. She makes me promise to call her every evening and to avoid dangerous trails in the rainy season. It is a small price to pay for her peace of mind.

followUps.q: Would you like to hike in another country?
followUps.answer: Very much. I would love to trek in Nepal one day, perhaps on one of the shorter routes in the Himalayas. The scenery there must be even more [[awe-inspiring]] than anything we have here.

note: Persona fix: Sirajganj is flat, so hiking now happens on trips to Sylhet and Bandarban with university friends ('cooped up in the city' replaced); added travel details and river walks between trips; added [[excursion]].
